source.citation: L'Hôpital, E., Lothenbach, B., Scrivener, K., Kulik, D. A. (2016). Alkali uptake in calcium alumina silicate hydrate (C-A-S-H). Cement and Concrete Research 85, 122-136.
source.location: Sections 2.1 to 2.3 (p. 123) and Appendices A, B and C

transcription.from: the published article (PDF), Appendices A to C, read from the text layer of the PDF
transcription.note: Section 2.2, p. 123: 'The amount of portlandite was quantified from the weight loss around 450 °C using the tangential method and the total water bound in the sample from the total water loss between 30 and 550 °C.' Recorded from 30 to 980 °C at 20 °C/min under N2. The tables were read from the text layer of the PDF, each value assigned to its column by its position on the page; the row structure (the Ca/Si blocks, the alkali solutions and the three times) was checked against the rendered pages, rows continued across a page break included. A value printed as an upper bound ('≤0.0037') is kept as that bound with the qualifier 'below_detection_limit'. A dash in Appendix B ('not observed') is left out, and so is the one cell printed empty (K at Ca/Si 1.2 in 0.05 M NaOH after 91 days). In Appendix C 'nm' (not measured) is null, a dash in a C-S-H column is null, and a dash in the portlandite column ('not observed') is written 0. The row 'NaOH 0.05 M, 364 days' of the C-A-S-H of Ca/Si 1.6 is printed twice in Appendix C, with alkali/Si -0.015 and -0.018 and nothing measured else; both are kept. The C-S-H columns of the last block of Appendix C carry a superscript 1 the article does not explain. In the block of Al/Si 0.1 of Appendix B the sample in 0.5 M NaOH prints its alkali, 458, under K and a dash under Na: kept as printed, so that no sodium is read for that sample.

bound_water_lower.description: Lower end of the temperature range whose weight loss is the total bound water.

bound_water_upper.description: Upper end of the temperature range whose weight loss is the total bound water.

temperature.description: 20 °C, synthesis and equilibration in a N2-filled glove box

water_solid_ratio.description: water-to-solid mass ratio of every sample: 2 g of CaO, SiO2 and CaO·Al2O3 in 90 mL of water or alkali hydroxide solution (Appendix A)

solution_volume.description: volume of solution each sample was prepared in

alkali_si_error_at_0_5_M.description: error of the alkali/Si ratio by the indirect method in 0.5 mol/L KOH, from a 50 mmol/L error on the dissolved concentration, at Ca/Si 1.0

concentration_relative_error.description: relative error of the ion chromatography, at most 10 % of the measured value

mixing_proportions.location: Appendix A, mixing proportions, in g per 90 mL of solution (calcium oxide, silica fume and monocalcium aluminate)

pore_solution.location: Appendix B, dissolved concentrations by ion chromatography and OH- from the pH; K and Na are the article's normalized values, the measured dissolved concentration times the target initial concentration over the measured initial alkali concentration of the blank solution

pH.location: Appendix B, pH measured at room temperature, corrected to 20 °C, electrode calibrated against KOH solutions

solid_composition.location: Appendix C, the C-S-H: Ca/Si, Ca/(Si+Al) and Al/Si, H2O/Si (±0.3), and the K or Na over Si taken up, by the indirect method (mass balance on the dissolved concentration), which can come out negative at high alkali concentration; portlandite in wt.% by TGA

notes: Each sample is a separate batch equilibrated for the time given: the three times of a solution are three samples, not one sampled three times.

The authors compare the solutions with CSHQ in GEM-Selektor and find calcium lower than computed above 0.05 mol/L of alkali hydroxide at Ca/Si 0.6 and silicon higher than computed at Ca/Si 1.6 (Section 3.2, Fig. 10).
